title: Setup
description: Learn how to install and configure React Query in a React application.

data.text: Setting up React Query takes just a few steps: install the package, create a QueryClient, wrap your app with QueryClientProvider, and optionally configure defaults. This lesson walks you through each step.
Install @tanstack/react-query using npm or your preferred package manager. This is the only required dependency for core functionality.

data.title: Install @tanstack/react-query
data.content: Installing the core React Query package

data.text: Optional: install the DevTools package for a visual debugging panel during development.

data.title: Install DevTools (Optional)
data.content: Adding the React Query DevTools for debugging

data.text: The QueryClient is the central object that manages all queries, caches, and mutations. You create it once at the root of your application. It is safe to create multiple QueryClients, but most apps use a single instance.

data.title: Create QueryClient
data.content: Instantiating a QueryClient with default options

terms.definition: The central object in React Query that manages all query caches, executes queries, and exposes imperative methods like invalidateQueries and setQueryData.
The time window (in ms) during which cached data is considered fresh. While fresh, React Query will not refetch. Default is 0.
The time window (in ms) that unused cached data persists before being garbage-collected. Default is 5 minutes.
A React context provider that makes the QueryClient available to all hooks in the component tree via React Context.

data.text: Place QueryClientProvider at the root of your component tree so every useQuery and useMutation call can access the same cache.

data.title: Set Up React Query in Your App
data.description: Create a fresh React project (Vite or Create React App) and integrate React Query. Configure default options appropriate for a real application.
steps: Create a new React project using Vite: npm create vite@latest my-app -- --template react-ts
Create src/queryClient.ts with a QueryClient instance
Set staleTime to 5 minutes and gcTime to 30 minutes
Wrap your root App with QueryClientProvider in main.tsx
Run the app and confirm no errors in the console
data.expectedOutcome: A working React app with QueryClientProvider at the root and React Query configured with sensible defaults. The DevTools panel appears in development mode.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Create one QueryClient instance at the app root
Wrap your app with QueryClientProvider to share the cache
Configure default options like staleTime and gcTime at creation
Add ReactQueryDevtools for debugging during development
Setup is complete â€” no additional configuration required to start using useQuery
data.takeaway: React Query setup is minimal: one package, one QueryClient, one provider. You can start fetching data immediately after wrapping your app.
